independent_audit.root_cause: Production destroy deletes Python Tclcommands while after IDs remain queued. Retained single-root interpreter and causal group isolation reproduce missing-command errors; correct owner cancellation removes them. Standalone process exit masks them. Not solely a multi-root harness issue.
independent_audit.harness_error: Cross-widget root.after_cancel removed Tclcommand but left child Python ownership list, leading to duplicate delete. Corrected ONLY in diagnostics.
independent_audit.nondiagnostic_original_probe: multi_three_roots did not process events; zero errors is not a lifecycle PASS
limitations: Standalone defaultprocess exit did not show errors; actual user-visible impact in long-lived hosts depends on continued event processing.
Probe error/registration clocks are relative; destroy ordering is recorded by queue snapshots, no separate wall timestamp.
The final pump in multi_with_events consumes lastroot callbacks too, unlike402 process exit. Counts are state/queue dependent, not expected to equal12.
Worker was a real executor/poll but returned saved402state; no active scientific solver interruption was tested.
